Subject: Bulk audit extract / retention guarantees - initial questions

Mina,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our RFP scoring we need concrete, machine-readable answers on Redwood's ability to:

1) Produce bulk export of audit events for arbitrary time windows (min: 1 hour, max: 24 months).
2) Include full immutable event metadata (event_id, occurred_at, source_service, actor_id, request_id, full_payload).
3) Produce tamper-evidence (signatures / checksums) and a chain-of-custody manifest.
4) Support redaction/fuzzy-redaction on-demand with preserved provenance markers.
5) Deliver via S3-compatible transfer with delivery SLA and transfer assurances (multipart checksums, signed URLs).

Can you confirm supported export formats, max throughput for a single export job, expected delivery SLA for a 30TB harvest, and what metadata fields are guaranteed? Appreciate a sample manifest/ndjson extract if possible.

Thanks,
Alan Pierce
Director, Compliance Programs
Peregrine Financial

Hi Alan — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a short spec and a 2MB sample export (NDJSON) showing field-level examples. Karthik is looped in for throughput/engineering specifics.

Summary answers (short):
- Bulk export: supported. Arbitrary windows within retention bounds (we support retention up to 7 years on Dedicated/Private plans; hosted defaults 3 years but can be configured).
- Metadata: event_id, occurred_at (ISO8601), source_service, actor_id, actor_type, request_id, trace_id, event_type, resource_id, full_payload (JSON string), and internal_seq (monotonic index) are included by default.
- Tamper-evidence: each export package includes SHA256 checksums for files and a signed manifest; for Dedicated/Private customers we offer HSM-backed manifests (optional).
- Redaction: we support configurable redaction profiles (token-level redaction + pseudonymization) that add a provenance object for each redacted event indicating redaction_reason and redaction_version; original hashes are preserved in the manifest for verifiability.
- Delivery: S3-compatible destination via multipart upload; we publish multipart etags and a transfer report. Typical SLA for export job completion depends on data volume and plan (see doc).

I'll let Karthik fill in the throughput numbers and expected timelines for a 30TB harvest. Attached: redwood_bulk_export_spec_v1.pdf and sample_export_20260831.ndjson.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alan / team — engineering details below. TL;DR: we can complete a 30TB harvest to a customer S3 target within 36 hours on Dedicated capacity with a pre-warmed harvest node set; on Hosted plan timelines are longer and may be scheduled in a maintenance window. Throughput assumptions and constraints are listed.

Throughput and SLA (engineer view):
- Single export worker sustained write throughput: ~500 MB/s (to S3 target) with standard network plumbing; parallelized across N workers.
- Typical pre-warmed dedicated harvest cluster (N=140 workers) -> aggregate sustained ~70 GB/s peak; practical sustained for export jobs (including checksumming & packaging) ~18-30 GB/s depending on compression and encryption overhead.
- 30 TB (uncompressed) practical completion: ~24-36 hours with N=140 workers, 3x replication/manifesting overhead accounted.
- For hosted customers we offer an expedited paid harvest (accelerated window) or a scheduled export in a batching queue (expect 3-7 days depending on queue).

Export formats and guarantees:
- Formats: NDJSON (preferred), Parquet (row-grouped), and gzipped tar bundles. Each record in NDJSON includes the full set of metadata fields documented in the spec.
- Manifest: top-level JSON manifest with file checksums (SHA256), record counts, time window, schema version, and an HMAC-SHA256 signature. For Dedicated/Private we provide an optional PKCS7 signature using the customer's KMS/HSM.
- Provenance: internal_seq + origin_hash per record; if redaction is applied, an additional provenance_record is appended that references original_record_hash and redaction_method.

Operational notes:
- Exports are cold-run against immutable event logs; we provide a transfer report and a machine-readable chain-of-custody (COC) record.
- For very large harvests we recommend pre-staging a target S3 bucket with an account-level transfer role to avoid egress throttles.

If you want, we can provide a scoped export runbook and sample workload numbers for your retention window and projected event rates.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: RE: Bulk audit extract / retention guarantees - initial questions

Alan — quick responses inline below, and we can schedule a 30-minute tech walkthrough tomorrow to run through a sample COC JSON and manifest.

1) Stability: origin_hash is derived from an immutable event payload hash (SHA256 of canonicalized event JSON). That canonicalization + payload hashing is stable across runtime updates; only changes to the canonicalization schema would change the hash (we version the schema and include schema_version in the manifest). If we ever re-ingest or reprocess, we record prior_schema_version and prior_hashes in the manifest so you can reconcile.

2) HSM signing: we support both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS. For Redwood-managed HSM signing we publish the signing cert chain (root CA + intermediate) and maintain a rotation schedule; rotation events are announced 30 days in advance and a digest of prior manifests is provided for continuity. For customer-managed KMS we are able to sign using an external key via a signed attestation flow. We'll include cert metadata in the spec appendix.

3) Post-export redaction: yes — we support a delta-redact workstream. You initiate a redaction request referencing export_id; we run the redaction, produce a delta manifest listing redacted_record_ids and provenance entries, and provide both a redacted export bundle and a tamper-evident delta manifest.
